after.title: Preprint: Wearable Sensors Predict Exertion Without Changes in Pulse Rate for Frail End-Stage Kidney Disease Patients
after.authors: Deehring, M. E.; Lorenz, E. C.; Katzman, H. P.; Isac, R.; Sasangohar, F.; Dhala, A.; Yamagami, M.
after.abstract: End-Stage Kidney Disease (ESKD) patients require careful exertion monitoring during prehabilitation to ensure safety and efficacy. Traditional prehabilitation typically relies on heart rate to estimate physical exertion; however, this is problematic for ESKD patients due to their lower physical capacity and the high prevalence of beta-blocker prescriptions, which prevent typical heart rate responses during exercise. In this study, we investigated whether multi-modal wearable sensors could better predict the Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE) in (N=13) ESKD patients and (N=13) healthy older adult controls. We collected continuous physiological data--including pulse rate, electrodermal activity, skin temperature, and accelerometer data--using a commercial smartwatch during prehabilitation sessions. Using individualized machine learning pipelines, we compared regression models built solely on pulse rate against comprehensive multi-feature models. We found distinct differences between the groups: baseline pulse-rate models performed substantially worse for the ESKD cohort, whereas they maintained predictive validity for controls. Conversely, multi-feature models significantly improved predictive performance for ESKD participants, achieving a Root Mean Square Error of 1.33. Feature selection confirmed that ESKD models relied heavily on physiological data beyond pulse rate to compensate for the lack of cardiovascular variability. These results demonstrate that heart rate alone is an insufficient biomarker for this population, and that remote exertion monitoring for ESKD patients requires distinct, multi-modal predictive algorithms rather than those designed for healthy adults.

after.authors: Perez-Gonzalez, A.; Sanchez-Palacios, J.; Fernandez-Gonzalez, P.; Paris-Alemany, A.; Chamorro-Sanchez, J.; La Touche, R.
after.abstract: Objectives: To investigate changes in cervical muscle mechanical properties during tongue-pressure tasks and maximum intercuspation (MIC) in individuals with chronic neck pain and healthy controls, and to explore associations between these properties, cervical mobility, tongue pressure, pain intensity, and neck disability. Methods: Eighty-four adults participated, including 42 individuals with chronic neck pain and 42 healthy controls. Myotonometry assessed frequency, stiffness, logarithmic decrement, relaxation time, and creep in the sternocleidomastoid (SCM) and trapezius muscles during tongue-pressure tasks at 50%, 80%, and 100% of maximum tongue pressure (MTP) and during maximum intercuspation. Group-by-condition effects were examined using linear mixed-effects models. Exploratory correlations and cervical mobility assessments were conducted in a subsample of 36 participants. Results: Tongue-pressure conditions showed significant effects on cervical muscle mechanical properties in 19 of 20 mixed-effects models at the nominal significance level, particularly for frequency, stiffness, relaxation time, and creep. Maximum intercuspation was associated with changes in frequency and stiffness in both muscles, with additional changes in relaxation time and creep in the sternocleidomastoid. Group-by-condition interactions were generally nonsignificant, apart from an isolated interaction involving right trapezius logarithmic decrement. The neck pain group exhibited lower absolute tongue-pressure values at 80% and 100% of maximum tongue pressure. Exploratory analyses identified reduced cervical extension and rotation, together with associations between cervical mobility, myotonometric properties, pain intensity, and tongue pressure. Conclusions: Orofacial motor tasks were associated with changes in cervical muscle mechanical properties regardless of chronic neck pain status. Although clinical characteristics were associated with selected mechanical and functional measures, chronic neck pain did not consistently modify task-related cervical responses. These findings support functional interactions between cervical and orofacial systems. Keywords: Chronic neck pain; myotonometry; tongue pressure; maximum intercuspation; cervical muscles; motor control.

after.authors: Yue, Z.; Rich, M.; Bickham, D.
after.abstract: Purpose: To identify patterns of adolescents' reported exposure to sexual and relationship content on social media and examine their associations with permissive sexual attitudes and perceived barriers to condom use. Methods: In a cross-sectional online survey (January to February 2026), 1,124 US high school students aged 16 to 18 years rated their typical exposure to 20 content categories developed with Youth Advisory Board input. Network analysis identified content communities, latent profile analysis grouped adolescents by community-level exposure, and covariate-adjusted linear models compared attitudes across profiles. Results: Four content communities and 4 exposure profiles were identified. Adolescents in the High Overall Exposure profile (n = 299; 27.3%) reported frequent exposure across all content communities and had higher adjusted permissive sexual attitudes (difference, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.40 to 0.75; d = 0.69) and perceived condom-use barriers (difference, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.31 to 0.69; d = 0.61) than the Moderate General Exposure profile. Differences were attenuated but persisted after adjustment for sociodemographic characteristics, sensation seeking, religiosity, and social media time (0.39 and 0.38) and were robust to data-quality exclusions and correction for classification error. Discussion: Adolescents' exposure to sexual and relationship content on social media is patterned, and higher overall exposure is associated with attitudes relevant to condom use. Sexual health counseling may benefit from addressing the broader mix of messages adolescents encounter online.

after.title: Preprint: Causal Analysis of Gynecologic Disorders and Adult-Onset Psychiatric Conditions: Integrating Matched Cohort, Polygenic Risk Score, and Mendelian Randomization
after.authors: Ben Messaoud, k.; Asgel, Z.; Licciardi, F.; Janecka, M.
after.abstract: Background: Endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), and uterine fibroids are linked to psychiatric morbidity, but evidence on causality across the full psychiatric spectrum remains limited. Methods: We assessed associations between endometriosis, PCOS, uterine fibroids and adult-onset psychiatric conditions (schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders, mood disorders, anxiety and stress-related disorders) in UK Biobank female participants using three complementary approaches: a matched-pair cohort design, a polygenic risk score (PRS)-based cohort analysis, and bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Sensitivity analyses were performed to test robustness. Results: Endometriosis was associated with mood disorders (OR= 1.51, 95% CI 1.40, 1.63), anxiety and stress-related disorders (OR=1.49, 95% CI 1.38, 1.62), and behavioral syndromes with physical components (OR= 1.28, 95% CI 1.01, 1.62). Uterine fibroids were associated with mood disorders (OR=1.17; 95% CI 1.11, 1.23), anxiety and stress-related disorders (OR=1.40, 95% CI 1.34, 1.48), and behavioral syndromes (OR=1.29, 95% CI 1.12, 1.48). PCOS was associated with mood disorders (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32, 1.64) and anxiety and stress-related disorders (OR=1.79, 95% CI 1.62,1.99), but not behavioral syndromes. No gynecologic disorder was associated with schizophrenia or other psychotic disorders. Genetic analyses supported shared liability and causal effects between fibroids and anxiety disorders. Conclusions: Women with gynecologic disorders are at increased risk of mood and anxiety- and stress-related disorders, and those with endometriosis or fibroids also face additional risk of behavioral syndromes. At least some of these risks appear driven by genetic liability, supporting routine mental health screening in gynecologic care and integrated treatment of gynecologic and mental health.

after.authors: Moustaklis, A.; Gerasimou, I.; Sotirakis, C.; Chairta, P.; Kurtis, M. M.; Del Campo, N.; Feige, T.; Schnalke, N.; Almarcha Menargues, M.-L.; Michailidou, K.; Christodoulou, K.; Fabbri, M.; Falkenburger, B. H.; Hadjileontiadis, L.; Hadjidimitriou, S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, Thessaloniki, Greece
after.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is associated with sleep and motor function impairment, even in the early stages. Here, we investigated whether passive wearable-based sleep and activity tracking can detect PD and its associated pathological hallmarks, dopaminergic deficit and -synuclein pathology. Sleep and activity metrics (SAM) were derived from free-living wrist accelerometry data of a U.S. cohort and used to train a machine learning model (SAM-PD) to distinguish persons with PD (n = 133) from healthy controls (n = 26). The model achieved an AUROC of 0.93 and an AUPRC of 0.98, demonstrated excellent test-retest reliability, and generalized without retraining to an independent European cohort (n = 40; 50% PwPD) monitored with a different device (AUROC, 0.95; AUPRC, 0.95). REM sleep duration, walking cadence, and low-level acceleration features were most predictive. Applied to a U.S. at-risk cohort, SAM-PD performed comparably to the resource-intensive Movement Disorder Society (MDS) prodromal PD risk score in detecting dopaminergic deficit (AUROC, 0.86 vs. 0.80; AUPRC, 0.45 vs. 0.46; n = 121; 12.4% prevalence) and -synuclein pathology (AUROC, 0.76 for both; AUPRC 0.50 vs. 0.42; n = 114; 16.7% prevalence). A combination with the MDS score modestly improved detection. Findings support further evaluation of wearable monitoring for PD screening and biomarker enrichment in larger populations.

after.authors: Reddy, S. P.; Chavez Neyra, A.; Lugo, K.; Ayzanoa, B.; Cucho Espinoza, C.; Morgenroth-Rebin, J.; Bocanegra, O. A.; Cuicapuza Arteaga, D.; Saavedra, M.; Gerungan, C.; Zorn, K. after.abstract: Background: Central nervous system (CNS) infections are a major cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries such as Peru. However, their epidemiology is poorly characterized due to a wide range of endemic and opportunistic pathogens involved and limited access to specialized neurodiagnostic testing. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) can detect any pathogen in a single hypothesis-free assay but has largely been confined to reference laboratories in high-income countries due to high cost and infrastructure requirements. We piloted an in-country, research-based CSF mNGS protocol in Lima, Peru, as a proof-of-concept study to assess the feasibility of implementing this approach in a resource-limited setting. Methods: Adults admitted with suspected CNS infection at Hospital Nacional Dos de Mayo, a large public hospital in Lima, were enrolled from August 2024 to April 2025, and approximately 0.5-2 mL of surplus CSF was collected. CSF mNGS (DNA and RNA) was performed in-country on a benchtop sequencer with half-volume library reactions and cloud-based analysis (CZID). Paired sequencing at a significantly higher depth was performed on a subset of samples in the United States for validation. Results: Among 43 participants (median age 48 years; 21% living with HIV), mNGS performed in Peru detected 20 pathogens in 18 samples (42%), of which 65% were not identified by routine clinical testing. Nine of 15 patients treated empirically for tuberculous meningitis were found to have a non-mycobacterial infection. Detected organisms included Toxoplasma gondii, Taenia solium, Treponema pallidum, human T-lymphotropic virus 1, herpesviruses, and, on deeper sequencing, Venezuelan equine encephalitis virus. Deep sequencing yielded 3.7-fold (DNA) and 6.9-fold (RNA) more reads and recovered four pathogens missed at shallower-depth. Conclusions: In-country CSF mNGS was feasible in Lima, Peru and recovered a clinically and epidemiologically meaningful spectrum of CNS pathogens, most missed by routine testing. By utilizing available, lower-output sequencers, we overcame a principal barrier to deploying this technology where the burden of undiagnosed CNS infection is greatest.

after.title: Preprint: Acute Dose-Response Effects of Guarana and Caffeine on Cognitive Performance in Healthy Adults
after.authors: Huang, Z.; Lee, T.; Gurney, T.; Desai, T.
after.abstract: Guarana (Paullinia cupana) is a fruit native to the Brazilian Amazon. It exerts potential cognitive-enhancing effects, primarily attributed to its caffeine content and additional bioactive compounds. However, the dose-response relationship of guarana and its comparative effects on cognitive performance to caffeine remain unclear. This double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised crossover study aimed to investigate the acute effects of guarana at three different doses (containing 1, 2, and 4 mg*kg*bodyweight-1 caffeine) compared to matched-dose caffeine (4 mg*kg*bw-1) and placebo on cognitive performance. Nineteen healthy adults completed one baseline assessment and five experimental sessions on six different days, each one week apart. During each experimental session, participants consumed one of the five supplement drinks in a randomised order. Four different cognitive tasks (memory, simple reaction time, sustained attention, and inhibition tasks) were performed pre-ingestion and 30 minutes post-ingestion to assess cognitive performance. Reaction time and number of errors in tasks were recorded, and data were analysed using a repeated measures analysis of variance. A significant main effect of session was found for memory (p = 0.05) and sustained attention (p = 0.01). However, no significant main effects of treatments, times, or treatment-by-time interactions were observed on reaction time or number of errors in all variables (p > 0.05). Guarana ingestion was not significantly different to matched-dose caffeine or placebo, and no dose-response relationship was observed for memory, simple reaction time, sustained attention, and inhibition tasks. Further research is warranted to explore chronic use, individual variability, and underlying physiological mechanism of guarana.

after.title: Preprint: Perioperative Safety, Surgical Morbidity, and Survival Outcomes of Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy (NACT-IDS) versus Primary Debulking Surgery (PDS) in Elderly Patients with Advanced Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
after.authors: Rafiee, A.; Boroumand, M. A.; Taghipour Zahir, S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: shahid sadoughi university of medical sciences
after.abstract: Abstract Background: Advanced epithelial ovarian cancer disproportionately affects older women. While primary debulking surgery (PDS) is the traditional gold standard, it carries substantial morbidity and mortality risks in frail, older patients. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking surgery (NACT-IDS) can downstage disease and mitigate these surgical risks, but high-level evidence syntheses specific to geriatric populations remain limited. Methods: This systematic review and meta-analysis adhered to PRISMA 2020 guidelines and was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261461644). Five electronic databases and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched for comparative studies evaluating NACT-IDS versus PDS in women aged [≥] 70 years (or [≥] 65 years in defined geriatric cohorts) with FIGO Stage IIIC/IV epithelial ovarian cancer. Outcomes were synthesized using random-effects models. Methodological quality was assessed via the ROBINS-I tool, cumulative evidence reliability via Trial Sequential Analysis (TSA), and overall evidence certainty via the GRADE framework. Results: Eleven retrospective cohort studies encompassing over 16,500 older patients met the inclusion criteria. NACT-IDS yielded an 80% reduction in unadjusted 30-day perioperative mortality compared to PDS (RR = 0.20, 95% CI [0.05, 0.89], p = 0.034). Furthermore, NACT-IDS significantly decreased hospital length of stay (MD = -3.12 days, p = 0.0044) and increased the likelihood of complete macroscopic resection (R0 = 0 cm) by 74% (RR = 1.74, 95% CI [1.01, 3.02], p = 0.047). Severe complications (Clavien-Dindo [≥] 3) trended lower with NACT-IDS (RR = 0.38, 95% CI [0.13, 1.08]). Unadjusted overall survival models demonstrated a 13% increased hazard of death for NACT-IDS (HR = 1.13, 95% CI [1.04, 1.23]); however, this primarily reflects profound selection bias (confounding by indication) where the frailest patients were systematically triaged to the NACT-IDS pathway. The overall certainty of evidence was appraised as Very Low. Conclusion: For older women with advanced epithelial ovarian cancer, NACT-IDS significantly improves perioperative safety, accelerates hospital recovery, and maximizes complete resection rates compared to upfront PDS. While retrospective survival data are heavily skewed by channeling bias, NACT-IDS effectively protects physiological reserve and should be strongly considered as the standard initial management strategy for this vulnerable demographic.

after.title: Preprint: Diet Soda Consumption is Associated with Shifts in Gut Microbiome Function of Overweight Young Women
after.authors: Appiah, P. Y.; Perez-Losada, M.; Sylvestsky, A. C.; Ortega-Santos, C. P.; Crandall, K. A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Exercise and Nutrition Sciences, Milken Institute School of Public Health, The George Washington University, Washington, DC, 20052
after.abstract: Background: Low-calorie sweeteners (LCS) are consumed as sugar substitutes and may alter gut microbial composition. Their effects on microbial functional pathways and cardiometabolic physiology in humans remain poorly understood, particularly among individuals with overweight. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis of an 8-week, single-arm pre/post intervention involving eight overweight young adult women who consumed sucralose- and acesulfame-potassium-sweetened Diet Pepsi three times daily. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples was used to profile microbial functional pathways with HUMAnN2. Multivariable linear mixed models (MaAsLin2) assessed associations between pathways and metabolic biomarkers. We hierarchically clustered nominally significant pathways into six representative groups and calculated Spearman correlations with interleukin-6 (IL-6), leptin, and HOMA-IR. P values were adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure. Biomarkers were measured using clinical chemistry and immunoassays. Results: MaAsLin2 identified 33 microbial pathways nominally associated with the intervention (exploratory FDR [≤] 0.25); one pathway (PWY-5104) also met the conventional FDR [≤] 0.10 threshold. Eighteen pathways were upregulated and 15 downregulated, with log fold changes ranging from -2.47 to 3.18. The 33 pathways were grouped into six functional clusters. L-alanine biosynthesis (PWY0-1061) was positively correlated with circulating IL-6 ({rho} = 0.74; q < 0.01). Phosphopantothenate biosynthesis I (PANTO-PWY) was not significantly correlated with IL-6 ({rho} = -0.46; q = 0.22). Conclusion: Gut microbial functional analysis identified a positive association between L-alanine biosynthesis and circulating IL-6. This finding complements previously reported taxonomic shifts in this cohort and suggests a potential relationship between LCS consumption, microbial function, and host inflammatory signaling.

after.authors: Perez, K.; Mak, J. K. L.; Tan, K. C. B.; Ganna, A.; Ceschi, A.; Jylhava, J.; Cheung, C.-L.; Alimonti, A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Institute of Oncology Research (IOR), Bellinzona, Switzerland
after.abstract: Observational studies sometimes report that individual medications are associated with lower mortality, but such signals are rarely compared across drugs and health systems. We screened prescription medications for associations with all-cause mortality using time-dependent Cox models in six cohorts from the UK, US, Finland, Hong Kong and Japan (8.93 million individuals aged 40 years or older; 1.49 billion prescriptions). Most medications were associated with higher mortality, reflecting confounding by indication. A few medications showed inverse associations with mortality, notably the varicella-zoster virus (VZV) vaccine, the antimalarials atovaquone-proguanil (Malarone) and mefloquine, and the hormone replacement therapy estradiol. These associations were only modestly attenuated by adjustment for comorbidity, lifestyle and socio-economic factors, and persisted within strata defined by pre-existing disease. While adjustment for self-reported health abolished the Malarone association, probably reflecting a healthy traveler profile, the VZV association was maintained. In FinnGen, deaths from external causes, which vaccination cannot prevent, were lower among VZV vaccine users, but much less so than all-cause mortality. In a target trial emulation in All of Us, the VZV association was maintained against matched unvaccinated individuals (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.53-0.70) and pneumococcal vaccine recipients (HR 0.64, 0.55-0.74), but was attenuated against recipients of tetanus-diphtheria vaccines, a group that also has low mortality (HR 0.85, 0.70-1.03). Healthy-user selection contributes to these signals but does not appear to fully explain the VZV vaccine association, which warrants confirmation in randomized trials. This multinational atlas provides a resource for prioritizing drug-repurposing candidates in ageing research.

after.title: Preprint: VectBox Sync: a web application for vectorcardiographic analysis of ventricular synchrony from 12-lead electrocardiograms
after.authors: Goldman, R.; Spagnuolo, D. N.; Chara, O.; Fernandez, J. M.
after.abstract: We introduce VectBox Sync, a browser-based application that implements a published vectorcardiographic (VCG) dyssynchrony index for exploratory assessment of ventricular electrical synchrony from the 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG). Despite guideline-directed patient selection, a substantial fraction of patients who receive cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) do not obtain the expected benefit. QRS duration and morphology remain the principal electrical criteria, yet they do not capture the three-dimensional trajectory of ventricular activation. VectBox Sync prioritizes native digital ECG recordings, including matrices and common clinical and research waveform formats; optional manufacturer-PDF import and externally digitized numerical files extend access when paper-like archives are the only available source. After optional preprocessing, the user selects a QRS interval, and the application calculates the dyssynchrony index relative to a calibrated control cutoff. It also provides companion VCG descriptors (voltage and speed integrals, loop angles, and planarity), together with VCG trajectories, synchrony-field maps, and a multilingual PDF report. Labeled conditions from the same session can be overlaid for comparison, for example across successive pacing settings. VectBox Sync makes this VCG-based assessment accessible through an integrated web application, providing quantitative descriptors that complement conventional ECG criteria. The application is available at https://vectbox.com/sync for research and educational use.

after.abstract: Aim: The oxygen uptake efficiency slope (OUES) is a prognostic indicator obtained from cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPX) in chronic heart failure (CHF) patients. Although various equations exist for calculating predicted OUES, it remains unclear whether absolute or percent-predicted values offer a more accurate prognostic assessment. To investigate and compare mortality prediction in CHF patients using the OUES absolute values or the percent-predicted approach, incorporating the equations of Hollenberg, Buys, and Milani. Methods: Retrospective cohort study involving CHF patients evaluated at a tertiary university hospital between July 2013 and July 2023. All patients underwent maximal CPX and were followed in a specialized outpatient clinic. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. To compare the prognostic accuracy between different approaches, we performed receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression. Results: A total of 1.180 patients were included, 57% male, with a mean age of 55 {+/-} 12 years. The median follow-up was 5.0 years (IQR 3.0 to 7.2 years), resulting in 147 deaths (12.5%). The area under de curve (AUC) was 0.71 to 0.72 for males, and 0.60 to 0.63 for females, without statistical difference in the AUC between absolute and percent-predicted OUES. Different cut-offs were identified for each sex for predicting mortality and all OUES metrics remained independent predictors in multivariate models using sex and age. Conclusions: OUES, in both absolute and percent-predicted forms, demonstrated similar accuracy in predicting mortality in CHF, with sex-specific cut-offs influencing clinical assessment.

after.authors: Jeong, Y.; Arirangan, S.; Akimova, E.; Thompson, K. N.; Geurgas, R.; Liu, J.; Bajpai, A.; Malerbi, K. F.; Kukar Bond, K.; Granka, J. M.; Hicks, B.; Hinds, D. A.; Bell, R. K.; 23andMe Research Team,  ; Zhou, G.; Gao, B.; Zacher, M.; Grotzinger, A. D.; Ganna, A.; Nivard, M. G.; Verhulst, B.; Wedow, R.
after.abstract: The rapidly changing cultural contexts over the past century modified the genetic factors that influence smoking initiation (SI). Using data from nearly seven million respondents, we conducted genome-wide associations study (GWAS) meta-analyses stratified by sex and generation across European, East Asian, African American, and Latino genetic ancestry populations. Sex and generation, but not genetic ancestry, moderate both the SNP-based heritability estimates and associations with individual loci. Specifically, SI is more heritable in females and younger generations. Furthermore, the impact of both discrete policy changes that target smoking and the gradual cultural redefinition of smoking norms across sex and generation are captured within the patterns of cross-trait genetic correlations between SI and extant smoking-relevant phenotypes. Robust cross-ancestry genetic correlations allowed us to meta-analyze the results across subsamples, identifying 1,717 loci associated with SI, including both main and moderated associations for either moderator. Genome-wide heterogeneity analyses identified 45 sex-specific loci and 7 generation-specific loci with distinct associations with SI. Finemapping analyses highlighted 389 and 304 loci with distinct patterns of potential causal variants by sex and generation. Accordingly, sex- and generation-specific macrosocial contexts dynamically influence the genetic architecture of SI, underscoring the need to consider gene-environment interplay for health behaviors as societal norms evolve.

after.authors: Le Roux, C.; Kalich, B.; Muhammad, C.; Horn, D.; Orroth, K.; Boer, L.; Wang, M.-J.; Tahrani, A. A.; Avcil, S.; Nguyen, L.; Li, Z.-R.; Fabiano, S.; Gibson, C. M.; Kang, Y. M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Division of Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Metabolism, Mass General Brigham and Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA
after.abstract: Aims: Although pivotal trials have established efficacy in weight reduction during the use of GLP-1 based therapies, daily fluctuations in food-related experiences between scheduled assessments remain to be better characterized. We therefore aimed to assess day-to-day patterns in food noise, cravings, hunger, satiety, and fullness among adults receiving weekly semaglutide or tirzepatide for weight management. Materials and Methods: This prospective, direct-to-participant, US observational study enrolled adults receiving weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or tirzepatide for weight management with self-reported BMI [≥] 30 kg/m2 before treatment initiation. Participants completed daily 24-hour-recall electronic diaries assessing food-related experiences for 6 weeks. Each injection defined Day 1 of a new dosing cycle. Results: Of 275 enrolled participants, 237 (86%) were included in the analysis. Daily food noise prevalence ranged from 4.3% to 23.8% over 6 weeks, generally highest on dosing day, declining thereafter, and returning toward dosing-day levels by Day 7. Overall, 182 participants (76.8%) reported food cravings at least once over 6 weeks, with moderate craving intensity as most frequently reported (98/237 [41.4%]). Across the study period, mean visual analog scale (0-100) on cycle Days 1, 2, and 7 were 39.9, 31.1, and 41.6 for hunger; 66.3, 69.8, and 64.2 for satiety; and 62.0, 65.1, and 60.6 for fullness. Conclusions: Food noise, cravings, and hunger declined soon after GLP-1 based therapy administration and increased towards the end of the weekly interval, whereas fullness and satiety fluctuated less. Daily assessments may capture experiences missed by conventional trial visit schedules and may be particularly relevant as therapies with longer half-lives become available.

after.authors: Fierro-Marrero, J.; Gallego-Garcia, A.; Cabrera-Duran, L.; Martinez-Benito, S.; Paris-Alemany, A.; La Touche, R.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Basic Health Sciences, Universidad Rey Juan Carlos, Alcorcon, Spain
after.abstract:
Background: EMFRA is a brief scale developed to assess physical, cognitive, emotional, and social functioning in older adults. This study examined its initial psychometric properties.

Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 201 older adults aged [≥]65 years without a diagnosis of dementia, recruited from the community, day-care and nursing centres from Madrid. Dimensional structure was examined through bootstrap parallel analysis (PA), bootstrap exploratory graph analysis (EGA), and factor analysis (FA), followed by progressive item refinement. Internal consistency, test-retest reliability in a subsample (n = 22), SEM, MDC95, floor and ceiling effects, and associations with SPPB, MoCA, Barthel Index, and HADS were assessed.

Results: The 21-item version did not reproduce the four hypothesized domains, yielding a three- dimensional solution with limited stability. A nine-item version comprised two factors, Autonomy and Psychological Distress, although FA fit was limited (TLI = 0.80; RMSEA = 0.13). A low hierarchical omega (0.409) did not support a total score, whereas factor reliability was adequate ({omega} = 0.840 and 0.785). Test-retest ICCs were 0.82 and 0.78, with wide 95% CIs. No floor or ceiling effects were observed. Autonomy correlated with SPPB (r = 0.751), MoCA (r = 0.697), and Barthel (r = 0.56), and Psychological Distress with HADS (r = 0.625).

Conclusions: The nine-item EMFRA shows preliminary evidence of a two-factor structure whose factors should be scored separately. Its temporal reliability and measurement error remain uncertain, and external validation is required before clinical implementation.

after.authors: Lohman, T.; Joyce, J.; Quiring, M.; Lashin, B.; Kapoor, A.; Engstrom, A. C.; Law, K.; Ferrer, F.; Contreras, L.; Alitin, J. P.; Gaubert, A.; Rodgers, K.; Head, E.; Malhas, R.; Pahlevan, N.; Nation, D. A.
after.abstract:
IntroductionElevated blood pressure variability (BPV) is predictive of Alzheimers disease neuropathologic change observed with AD biomarkers. However, prior studies have largely focused on visit-to-visit BPV, which may be influenced by antihypertensive medication adherence and other external factors. Few studies have investigated beat-to-beat BPV, a reliable and direct measure of cardiovascular and autonomic function relevant to AD.

MethodsIndependently living older adults (N=132) were recruited from the community. Participants underwent continuous blood pressure monitoring and venipuncture. Plasma p- Tau217, p-Tau181, GFAP, NfL, and amyloid-{beta}42/40 ratio were assessed. Linear regression examined the relationship between beat-to-beat systolic BPV and plasma AD biomarkers with and without adjustment for age, sex, systolic blood pressure, and apolipoprotein E4 (APOE4) carrier status.

ResultsElevated beat-to-beat BPV was associated with elevated plasma p-Tau217 ({beta}=0.32, p=0.008), plasma p-Tau181 ({beta}=0.22, p=0.05), and plasma GFAP ({beta}=0.41, p=0.00001). Elevated BPV was not associated with plasma amyloid-{beta}42/40 ratio or plasma NfL.

DiscussionIncreased beat-to-beat BPV is associated with increased Core 1 T1 biomarkers of phosphorylated and secreted AD tau in blood plasma (i.e., pTau217, pTau181), but not with amyloid-{beta}42/40 ratio, a biomarker more exclusively indexing cerebral amyloid retention alone.

Elevated BPV was also associated with higher plasma GFAP, a marker of astrocyte reactivity. These findings are consistent with prior studies relating visit-to-visit BPV to AD biomarkers, suggesting that intrinsic cardiovascular and/or autonomic factors underlie links between BPV and AD.

after.authors: Kittrell, H. D.; Kauffman, J.; Smit, R. A. J.; Atabaki, N. N.; Merino, J.; Walker, R. W.; Loos, R. J. F.; Nadkarni, G. N.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
after.abstract: Introduction. Diet quality scores are well-established predictors of cardiometabolic health but compress an individuals food intake into a single dimension, potentially masking dietary variation relevant to disease risk. Whether this hidden variation carries prognostic information has not been tested at scale. Methods. We applied non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to the reported intake of 148 individual foods and beverages from 87,162 UK Biobank participants. We tested the association of NMF-derived intake factors with incident coronary artery disease (CAD), type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) over a median 9.4 years of follow-up using Cox proportional hazards models. We evaluated the prognostic value of the factors beyond diet quality scores using stepwise Cox models and net reclassification improvement (NRI), and characterized their metabolic profiles through metabolome-wide association analyses (MWAS) of 249 circulating metabolites. Results. NMF identified eight reproducible intake factors that were stable across geographically distinct samples. Four factors were significantly associated with incident cardiometabolic disease: a high sugar and processed foods factor was adversely associated with T2D (HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.11-1.27) and CKD (HR 1.15; 1.07-1.23), while a plant-based and fish factor was protective for CKD (HR 0.90; 0.84-0.96) and a cheese and whole grains factor was protective for CAD (HR 0.94; 0.90-0.98). The factors improved disease discrimination beyond both diet quality scores ({Delta}C up to +0.0049) and correctly reclassified 8-16% more individuals, whereas adding either score to models containing the factors produced negligible further improvement. The high sugar and processed foods factor was associated with depletion of omega-3 fatty acids and the plant-based and fish factor showed enrichment in polyunsaturated fatty acids. Conclusions. Food-level dietary intake profiling captures clinically relevant variation that established diet quality scores mask, offering a path toward more personalized dietary assessment for cardiometabolic disease prevention.

after.abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myocarditis affects up to 2% of patients on ICI and has up to a 50% mortality. Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential (CHIP) is a risk factor for ICI myocarditis. Objectives To leverage a multi-omics approach to evaluate cytokines associated with ICI myocarditis, immunosuppression resistance, CHIP in ICI myocarditis and implicated pathways and cell type contributions. Methods 236 cardio-oncology patients were enrolled, including 88 who were on ICI. Cytokine profiling from patients on ICI were sampled and analyzed using machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence. Single-cell multi-omics of peripheral blood from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63) evaluated cell-type contributions of cytokines and implicated pathways. Validation of Yale proteomic analyses was done using the Stanford CYTOF dataset. Results Top features associated with ICI myocarditis included IL13, CXCL10, PDGFA, CCL13, CCL17 and KITlg. Top KEGG pathways associated with ICI myocarditis and immunosuppression resistant ICI myocarditis included JAK STAT signaling, IL17 signaling and lipid/atherosclerosis pathways. At the single-cell level, the consensus signals distinguishing myocarditis from non-myocarditis across cohorts was predominantly driven by module-level JAK STAT, T cell, and Toll like receptor activation. Similar transcription gene programs were activated in CHIP carriers including modules implicated in the pro-inflammatory immune response, such as NF kappa B, IL17, MAPK, and TNF pathways within CHIP cells spanning lymphoid (cytotoxic CD8+ NKT, and natural killer cells) and myeloid lineages. Conclusions Across cohorts, JAK STAT signaling emerges as a convergent and potentially actionable axis in ICI myocarditis that is further amplified in CHIP carriers, supporting cytokine-guided risk stratification and JAK STAT directed immunosuppression as testable strategies.

after.author_corresponding_institution: Saw Swee Hock School of Public Health, National University of Singapore, Singapore
after.abstract: Introduction: Advance care planning (ACP) enables quality end-of-life (EOL) care that reflects patients' values and preferences. However, ACP remains limited among individuals with neurosurgical conditions -- such as stroke, glioma, or metastatic brain tumours -- who often experience rapid decline and short prognoses. When ACP discussions occur only after cognitive deterioration or acute events, opportunities for meaningful conversations are lost. This study aims to assess the baseline knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) of ACP among neurosurgical patients and their caregivers in Singapore. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of 30 patients with symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (SICH) or brain tumours at the National University Hospital and their caregivers. Using validated ACP engagement questionnaires, we assessed participants' KAP, and readiness on 5-point Likert scales (1 lowest - 5 best), alongside nine ACP knowledge statements. Results: Patients demonstrated below-average ACP knowledge (mean = 4.1 / 9) and largely neutral attitudes (3.2 / 5) and perceptions (3.1 / 5). Misconceptions were common, including beliefs that ACP documents are legally binding, that preferred care cannot be delivered without ACP, and that ACP is solely a doctor's responsibility. Consequently, both patients and caregivers showed low levels of ACP engagement. Conclusion: The findings highlight the need to introduce ACP education and conversations earlier in the care journey, especially for individuals at risk of cerebrovascular or cardiovascular events. Early engagement, particularly among those with hypertension or other risk factors, presents a crucial window for preparing patients and families for future care decisions.

after.authors: Choi, I. Y.; Jeon, Y.; Lee, I. K.; Kim, K.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Seoul National University College of Medicine
after.abstract: Background Pediatric out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) is a rare but devastating event. However, the extent to which large-scale public health interventions, such as COVID-19 social distancing policies, affected the incidence of pediatric OHCA remains unclear. Methods We conducted a nationwide interrupted time-series analysis using data from the Korea Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Registry (2008-2023). The primary outcome was the monthly incidence of OHCA among individuals aged 0-18 years. The study period was divided into three phases: pre-intervention (January 2008-February 2020), social distancing (March 2020-April 2022), and post-lifting (May 2022-December 2023). We used segmented Poisson regression, adjusted for population size and seasonal variation, to estimate changes in monthly incidence at each policy change and reported the results as incidence rate ratios (IRRs). To determine whether these changes differed by age, we compared children with adults (19-64 years) and elderly individuals ([≥]65 years). Results Of the 456,839 registry entries, 10,965 were pediatric OHCAs, of which 6,891 underwent resuscitation in the emergency department. The crude incidence was 7.04, 7.14, and 8.35 per 100,000 person-years in the three phases, respectively. Before the pandemic, incidence rose slightly (annual IRR 1.006 [95% CI 1.001-1.012]; P = 0.032). At the implementation of social distancing, incidence fell immediately (IRR 0.926 [95% CI 0.865-0.991]; P = 0.027), without a significant change in slope (P = 0.081). After restrictions were lifted, incidence rose immediately (IRR 1.138 [95% CI 1.048-1.235]; P = 0.002) and then declined gradually (monthly IRR 0.993 [95% CI 0.988-0.999]; P = 0.023). These changes were confined to children aged 1-11 years (implementation IRR 0.812 [95% CI 0.666-0.991]; post-lifting IRR 1.562 [95% CI 1.278-1.909]). The pattern of change differed significantly by age group (P < 0.001), mainly because incidence rose in children, but not in adults or elderly individuals, after restrictions were lifted. Conclusions Nationwide social distancing was associated with a transient decrease in pediatric OHCA incidence, which was concentrated among children aged 1-11 years and was followed by a rebound above the expected level after restrictions were lifted. Surveillance of pediatric OHCA should account for abrupt changes in children's daily environments, including the closure and reopening of schools and childcare facilities.

after.title: Preprint: Antimicrobial stewardship strategies to optimise antibiotic prescribing in primary care: physicians awareness, beliefs, and strategy use
after.authors: Borek, A. J.; Palacz-Poborczyk, I.; Kuzminska, J.; Luszczynska, A.; Kloda, K.; Babicki, M.
after.abstract: Background: National efforts to promote antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) and prevent antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in primary care need strengthening. Research supports clinician-targeted AMS strategies to optimise antibiotic prescribing, but implementing them in clinical settings is challenging. Aim: Assessment of primary care physicians' awareness of, use of, and beliefs about evidence-based AMS strategies, and perceived barriers and facilitators to implementing them in a country with high antibiotic consumption rates (Poland). Methods: A pre-registered observational survey study. Eligible physicians worked in primary care in Poland for 6+ months and were recruited via professional networks and social media. Data were collected through a pre-piloted online questionnaire and analysed descriptively. Results: 270 physicians (68.2% Specialists/Residents in Family Medicine) participated. Respondents were aware of the threat of AMR (88%), the importance of AMS (93%) and their role in AMS (89%). They most recognised, utilised, perceived as effective, and recommended rapid diagnostic tests, clinical guidelines, and scales/criteria. Respondents reported high familiarity but lower engagement with communication strategies, national actions, education/training, and campaigns. Delayed prescriptions were the least used and recommended. Main barriers were time constraints and insufficient awareness of which strategies to implement. Recommended strategies included tests, guidelines, scales/criteria, AMS action plans for general practices, patient communication resources, and promoting awareness of AMS and its role in high-quality care. Conclusion: Awareness and use of evidence-based AMS strategies among physicians working in Polish primary care clinics appear high. Improvements may require reaching disengaged physicians, increasing uptake of underutilised strategies, and strengthening the impact of already used strategies.

after.title: Preprint: Automatic classification of seizure adequacy in electroconvulsive therapy: A proof-of-concept study
after.authors: Panah, M.; Jessen, B. L.; Rand, A.; Jansen, T.; Jorgensen, M. B.; Morup, M.; Jorgensen, A.
after.abstract: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the most effective treatment of a range of severe mental dis-orders and is annually given to more than a million patients worldwide. Dosing of the electrical charge is critical for efficacy and side-effect burden; however, it is currently based on manual assessment of seizure quality and exhibits substantial clinical heterogeneity. Here, we collected 1,000 ECT session electroencephalograms (EEG) from 130 individual ECT patients and made an expert-level classification of the EEGs into actionable seizure quality categories (null-response [0], threshold [T], and adequate [A]). We then trained a range of machine learning algorithms on the raw EEG data to classify the EEGs into these categories and tested for classi-fication accuracy. The highest performing algorithm was able to classify the seizures with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of >0.9 for both the 0 vs. T and the T vs. A categories corresponding to excellent discrimination. In contrast, the accuracy of predicting seizure quality in subsequent treatments was only moderate. The addition of clinical variables to the models, such as demographics, anesthesia and anticonvulsant exposure, did not improve model performance. These results provide proof-of-concept of machine learning classification of seizure adequacy in ECT based on raw EEG data. The findings could pave the way for the de-velopment of more objective and personalized decision-support tools in ECT.

after.authors: Leguizamon, M.; Zhang, B. Y.; Custer, R. M.; Molinare, C. P.; Oyen, E.; Noriega-Makarskyy, D. T.; Axelrod, J.; Lim, A. C.; Wu, C.; Agarwal, M.; Salminen, L. E.; Choupan, J.; Mosqueda, L.; Han, S. D.
after.abstract: Background: Financial exploitation is a prevalent public health concern among older adults, and emerging evidence links vulnerability to gray matter macrostructure and white matter microstructure, including within brain regions and networks implicated in early Alzheimer's disease. Although diffusion tensor imaging is sensitive to age-related variation in brain microstructure, its scalar metrics cannot distinguish among the tissue properties contributing to observed differences. Neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging (NODDI) models distinct tissue compartments, yielding estimates of neurite density, dendritic complexity, and extracellular free water. Methods: This study examined associations between scam susceptibility and NODDI metrics using ultra-high-field 7-Tesla imaging in 116 older adults without dementia. Neurite density index (NDI), orientation dispersion index (ODI), and free-water fraction were quantified within seven a priori regions of interest linked to early Alzheimer's disease. Multivariate regressions evaluated associations between scam susceptibility and NODDI metrics, adjusting for age, sex, education, and global cognition, with multiple comparison correction within each metric. For significant regions, post-hoc hierarchical regression models tested whether NODDI metrics explained variance beyond regional cortical thickness, total gray matter, and total intracranial volume. Results: Greater scam susceptibility was associated with higher NDI ({beta}=0.30, pFDR=.025) and lower ODI ({beta}=-0.28, pFDR=.044) in the middle temporal gyrus (MTG). No other regions survived correction. Additionally, MTG NDI and ODI explained variance beyond macrostructure measures. Conclusions: These findings identify NODDI metrics as novel microstructural correlates of scam susceptibility beyond macrostructure, supporting investigation of their relevance to financial vulnerability in older age.

after.authors: Watson, F.; Sariyildiz, A.; Sayici, E. N.; Metin, O.; Kundakci, B.; Bull, A. M.; Kedgley, A.; Basaran, S.
after.abstract: Introduction: The 2023 Kahramanmaras-Turkiye earthquakes resulted in many paediatric amputations. While prosthetic provision following disasters has been described, little is known about longer-term physical and psychosocial outcomes in children with earthquake-related limb loss. Aim: Evaluate health-related quality of life, prosthesis experience, pain, and function approximately two years post-amputation. Method: Retrospective analysis was conducted of children with earthquake-related limb loss who attend the XXX Center. Socio-demographic and amputation-related data, psychological status, outcome scores for pain, the Paediatric Quality of Life Inventory (PedsQL) and the Trinity Amputation and Prosthesis Experience Scales (TAPES) were included. Results: Fifty-six children (50% female; 13.7{+/-}5.0 years old) were included. Children had unilateral upper limb loss (n=15), unilateral lower limb loss (n=31), bilateral lower limb loss (n=7), or combined upper and lower limb loss (n=3). Data were obtained 2.3{+/-}0.4 years following amputation. Median child-reported PedsQL scores were 72.3/100.0, with high social functioning (85.0/100.0) but lower emotional functioning (60.0/100.0). No differences in PedsQL outcomes were found between limb loss groups. Children rated their physical and emotional quality of life higher than carers rated them. TAPES median scores were 50.0/75.0 for psychosocial adjustment, 16.0/36.0 for activity restriction, and 34.5/45.0 for prosthetic satisfaction. Children with unilateral lower limb loss demonstrated superior adjustment and prosthetic satisfaction than children with unilateral upper limb or bilateral lower limb loss (p<0.05). Conclusions: Children demonstrated favourable physical, social, and school-related quality of life 2.3 years after the earthquakes. However, emotional wellbeing remained affected, highlighting the importance of long-term mental health support alongside prosthetic and rehabilitation services.

after.abstract: White matter hypointensity on T1-weighted MRI (T1-WMHypo), a putative marker of white matter pathophysiological changes, has been less systematically investigated than the widely studied T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (T2-FLAIR) hyperintensity lesions. Here, we built the lifespan normative reference and assessed the clinical significance of T1-WMHypo across various brain disorders using a large multicenter dataset. We first established lifespan normative reference for T1-WMHypo volume by 34,148 healthy individuals (aged 4-85 years). Then, in 7,587 patients across 21 neurological and psychiatric disorders, normative reference-derived deviations revealed disease-specific patterns, with marked deviations in neurological diseases. Deviations of T1-WMHypo volume contributed to differential diagnosis, larger deviations correlated with brain atrophy, cognitive impairment, and poorer outcomes in various brain disorders. Elevated burden of T1-WMHypo volume predicted poor medication response in Parkinson's disease and accelerated disability progression in multiple sclerosis. These associations persisted after adjusting for conventional T2-FLAIR hyperintensity lesions. T1-WMHypo deviations provide an individualized marker of white matter pathophysiological changes, offering novel insights for precision medicine across development, aging and brain disorders.

after.title: Preprint: DxToniaNet: A Neural Network for Estimating the Severity of Leg Dystonia in Children with Cerebral Palsy
after.authors: Bajpai, R.; Rust, A.; Lott, E.; Kim, S.; Gandham, S.; Chintalapati, K.; Blackburn, J.; Gelineau-Morel, R.; Kruer, M. C.; Mingbunjerdsuk, D.; O'Malley, J.; Tochen, L.; Waugh, J. L.; Wu, S.; Feyma, T.; Perlmutter, J. S.; Aravamuthan, B. R.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, Washington University School of Medicine, St. Louis, MO, USA
after.abstract: Importance: Leg dystonia affects 50-80% of children with cerebral palsy (CP), but severity assessment remains subjective and time-consuming. Objective tools are urgently needed to quantify leg dystonia severity in clinical care and clinical trials. Objective: To develop and validate a deep neural network (DxToniaNet) for leg dystonia severity estimation using 2D clinical video recordings. Design, Setting, and Participants: We retrospectively analyzed video recordings of 298 children with cerebral palsy undergoing a seated hand open-close task as part of routine clinical care (Center 1: 193 videos, 720p/30fps; Center 2: 105 videos, 4K/60fps). Videos were rated for leg dystonia severity by a group of 7 experts using the Global Dystonia Rating Scale (GDRS) leg subscore (range 0-40) which has a minimum clinically important difference (MCID) of 4 points. Videos displaying leg dystonia (median expert GDRS score [≥]1) were used to develop and test a machine learning model (DxToniaNet) for estimating leg dystonia severity. Open-source software (OpenPose) estimated bilateral knee, ankle, and toe coordinates, normalized for height and camera positioning, and 69 variance and amplitude features were calculated based on established expert-cited features of leg dystonia. A neural network, DxToniaNet, was developed, trained and validated using 5-fold cross-validation on Center 1 videos before final testing on independent Center 2 videos. Main Outcome(s) and Measure(s): Mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and accuracy in differentiating between videos with clinically meaningful differences in GDRS scores were calculated relative to experts' median GDRS scores. Results: When estimating experts' leg GDRS scores in testing data, the proposed machine learning (ML) model yielded a MAE of 1.71 {+/-} 1.68 and RMSE of 2.21 {+/-} 0.34 (significantly less than the GDRS MCID of 4), and 90-94% accuracy in differentiating between videos with greater than a 4-point difference in the GDRS. Conclusions and Relevance: We have demonstrated that DxToniaNet can accurately estimate leg dystonia severity compared to experts' assessments with a small (clinically insignificant) error margin. Our methodology supports generalizability since DxToniaNet was developed and tested using independent videos datasets from different centers, recorded under different conditions. In the future, DxToniaNet may help facilitate standardized leg dystonia severity estimation in clinical care and clinical trials.

after.title: Preprint: How inherited variation shapes human disease trajectories
after.authors: Urbut, S. M.; Truong, B.; Khurshid, S.; Hornsby, W.; Rehm, H. L.; Ellinor, P.; Natarajan, P.; Parmigiani, G.; Gusev, A.
after.abstract: Although inherited variation is fixed at birth, its effects on health change with age and differ between common and rare variants. Here, we introduce Mendelnoulli, a longitudinal model that combines the age-dependent effects of polygenic and monogenic variation on health records, separating how much disease each individual accumulates overall from diseases to which they are prone. Mendelnoulli further allows polygenic and monogenic components to exert different influences on latent disease trajectories. We apply the model to 348 diseases, 36 polygenic scores, and 34 monogenic conditions across three biobanks and provide an atlas of the age-dependent effects of inherited variation on common human diseases. We show that polygenic effects change significantly with age, with Mendelnoulli improving held-out one-year discrimination for all 28 diseases tested compared with a model whose polygenic effects are constant over age (median AUC 0.95 vs 0.92). For individuals with no prior diagnoses, Mendelnoulli identified 8.6 more of every 100 new cases than that model, when each flagged the 5\% at highest risk. For genes with an established disease, Mendelnoulli selected that disease for 27 of 30 genes and ranked it first for 17 (7 expected by chance), and recovered known differences in timing, such as earlier breast cancer effects for BRCA1 than BRCA2 (peak 48 vs 66 years). Mendelnoulli provides a unified model of common and rare genetic influences on disease trajectories across the life course.

after.title: Preprint: "Wow, this could be massive": Donor-Conceived Families Experience with Unexpected Recontact for Risk of Inherited Cardiac Conditions
after.authors: Mitchell, L. A.; Ruscigno, A.; Mulhern, S.; Yeates, L.; Macciocca, I.
after.abstract: Introduction: Recontacting families post-gamete donation, after a genetic diagnosis is made in the donor, can create complex challenges for healthcare providers and families. However, there is little literature that explores the family experience. This study aimed to explore the experiences of parents and donor-conceived young people navigating the recontact process and undergoing predictive genetic testing for an inherited cardiac condition. Methods: Semi-structured interviews were conducted to explore participants' experiences in unexpectedly being recontacted and undergoing predictive genetic testing for an inherited cardiac condition. Interviews were recorded and transcribed verbatim. A reflexive thematic analysis was performed. Results: Thirteen participants agreed to be interviewed, nine were parents and four were donor conceived young people. Four overarching themes were identified: (1) Out of the Blue, (2) A ripple effect on the family, (3) Calm after the storm, (4) Beneath the Ripples: the psychological impact. Discussion: Interviews provided insights into fertility services recontact and the predictive genetic testing process. From the themes, we conceptualize a ripple effect model. Findings highlight how cardiac genetics and fertility services are evolving, and the critical role of genetic counselors. The recontact process affects the entire family. However, most participants adapted and moved forward from this event.

after.title: Preprint: Ontology-Based SEA-CDM Integration for Vaccine Clinical Trials: Query, Similarity, and Design Recommendation
after.authors: Zhu, J.; Yeh, F.-Y.; Zheng, J.; He, Y.
after.abstract: ClinicalTrials.gov provides valuable information for vaccine research, but fragmented data structures and inconsistent vaccine naming complicate systematic cross-trial analysis. The Study-ExperimentAssay Common Data Model (SEA-CDM) provides a standardized structure for biomedical study data, while biomedical ontologies supply semantic relationships among concepts. We extracted 9,147 vaccinerelated study records from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT) database, mapped their records into SEA-CDM, and linked vaccine products and reported adverse events (AEs) to the Vaccine Ontology (VO) and Ontology of Adverse Events (OAE), respectively. Building on the existing Ontology-based SEA Network (OSEAN), we organized the integrated data into relational tables and a Neo4j knowledge graph while retaining links to original registrations. We evaluated three applications to assess semantic trial retrieval, context-aware AE ranking and trial similarity, and trial design recommendation. First, VO-based query expansion retrieved 41 candidate RNA vaccine trials compared with 16 using exact VO identifier matching. Second, a context-aware AE ranking model incorporating SEA-CDM features and VO-derived vaccine families improved recall@10 from 0.317 to 0.383 over a frequency-based baseline. TransE and CompGCN embeddings achieved Hits@10 of 0.950 and 0.946, respectively, for retrieving trials sharing the same VO identifier within disease-specific candidate sets. Third, an ontology-based clinical trial design recommendation model was developed using several machine learning methods under leave-one-Material-out evaluation across 23 vaccine classes, although performance varied across classes. These findings demonstrate how structural and semantic integration can support multiple clinical trial analyses using vaccine studies as a case study. This framework provides a foundation for extending ontology-supported data integration and analysis to other clinical research domains.

after.title: Preprint: Reliability-Aware Clinical Relation Learning for Uncertainty-Robust Multi-Label Chest X-ray Classification
after.authors: Jin, Y.; Liu, T.; stephen, m.
after.abstract: Background: Automated multi-label classification of chest radiographs is complicated by overlapping imaging findings, noisy report-derived labels, and changes in disease co-occurrence across clinical settings. Existing clinical-hierarchy methods can encode label relationships, but a rigid hierarchy may conflate categorical membership with empirical association and propagate annotation errors. Methods: We investigated Reliability-Aware Clinical Relation Learning (ReCaRL), a graph-assisted framework for multi-label chest radiograph classification. An image encoder produces initial finding scores, while a graph constructed from training-label associations provides reliability-weighted, confidence-gated updates. Uncertain annotations are handled with observation masks. The evaluation compares flat, weighted, graph-based, and hierarchy-penalty baselines, with internal and external discrimination and calibration assessments. Results: In the internal evaluation, ReCaRL achieved macro AUROC 0.821 and macro AUPRC 0.437, compared with 0.812 and 0.423 for the masked/weighted baseline. Mean AUROC across five common findings was 0.865 versus 0.858. External testing yielded AUROC 0.799 and AUPRC 0.409. Post-hoc calibration reduced the internal Brier score from 0.113 to 0.102 and the external expected calibration error from 0.082 to 0.061, without changing AUROC or AUPRC. Conclusions: Reliability-aware graph propagation and confidence gating were associated with modest improvements in multi-label chest radiograph classification relative to the matched masked/weighted baseline. Post-hoc calibration improved probability reliability in the reported evaluations. The findings do not establish a benefit in prospective clinical decision-making.

after.title: Preprint: Enrollees and Early Lessons from an Agentic Healthcare Platform with Physicians in the Loop
after.authors: Shen, Z.; Ramachandran, A.; Hsiang, E.; Gill, J.; Miller, R.; Stark, N. R.
after.abstract: Agentic healthcare platforms that combine large language models with physician oversight are growing quickly, but little is known about who uses them. We characterized 3,223 enrollees of Lotus AI, a free, physician-supervised agentic platform, who completed onboarding, messaged the agent, and had a linked health record between February and July 2026, and compared them with national benchmarks. Median age was 51 years and 62% were male. Chronic condition prevalence exceeded 2024 National Health Interview Survey estimates in every age band by 4 to 7 percentage points; 18% had a functional or symptom-defined disorder; among the 30% with four or more ambulatory visits in the prior year, care was spread across nearly five providers, with 44% meeting a threshold for high fragmentation. Users with functional disorders generated 1.8 times as many physician escalations and 2.6 times as many laboratory orders as other users, but no more prescriptions. This profile differs from the younger, predominantly female populations reported for direct-to-consumer telemedicine. It moves chronic disease management, functional disorder pathways, and care coordination from aspirations to design requirements, and we argue that deployed AI care platforms should characterize their populations against national benchmarks early.
